A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTS-VAR work. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Infinity-2B experiments on GenEval and T2I-CompBench, computational analyses, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Infinity-8B, DPG-Bench, human preference, diversity, computational-cost, and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain adaptive descending batches, early DINOv2/K-Means++ clustering, and late potential-based resampling. The additional implementation disclosures and Infinity-8B configuration introduce no new algorithmic component or selection procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds DPG-Bench evaluation in Appendix D and human assessment of 15 image groups in Section 5.3. These extend benchmark and human-evaluation coverage within text-to-image generation; GenEval and T2I-CompBench remain. Infinity-8B itself changes model configuration rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: The original GenEval and T2I-CompBench comparator sets remain. The new DPG-Bench comparison includes HART and PixArt-Sigma, neither previously evaluated in the paper. Table 14 also introduces random dropping as a clustering control. Infinity-8B comparisons reuse raw inference, IS, and BoN.

E3.justification: New protocols include Infinity-8B at 512 pixels with a ten-scale schedule, randomized image ordering in a study yielding 21 questionnaires and 315 selections per criterion, four-image-per-prompt DPG evaluation, CLIP-Div measurement, and timing/peak-memory evaluation. Appendix G.2 excludes image decoding from timing and uses two inference passes for BoN at N=8. These additions do not establish changes to the retained Infinity-2B experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds output-diversity analysis, component-level runtime and memory analysis, and clustering versus random dropping while retaining resampling (Tables 10, 12, and 14). It extends temperature sensitivity to lambda=50 and 100 and adds fixed-batch-size 2 and 4 profiles in Figure 2. The earlier scale, potential, extractor, reward-model, and pipeline ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 does not specify seeds. v2 Appendix B discloses seeds 0–3 and GPU-process seed offsets; Appendix D specifies four DPG images using seeds 0–3. This is newly documented seed information, not evidence of increased repeated runs. Confidence intervals, error bars, and formal significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables are retained, while substantial results are added. Infinity-8B reaches 0.8188 GenEval in Table 1 versus 0.7646 raw and 0.7995 BoN at N=4; Appendix Table 8 inconsistently prints 0.8189. DPG-Bench reports 82.94 for TTS-VAR versus 82.52 BoN and 81.72 raw Infinity. New tables report human votes, diversity, runtime/memory, and further ablations; Figure 2 revises memory profiles. These extend results rather than demonstrate improved scores for the original runs.

T1.justification: Section 3 introduces a non-equivalent indexing error: Equation 1 changes the summand from up(r_i) to up(r_k) while still summing over i. Its accompanying text also changes accumulation over the first k residuals to all K residuals. The unchanged algorithm indicates a formal-description error rather than a new method. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claimed first general test-time scaling framework for VAR, its stage-specific diversity/selection contributions, and the 0.69-to-0.75 GenEval improvement. Explicitly naming Infinity-2B in the abstract clarifies the existing result rather than changing the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the diversity measurements as showing little diversity sacrifice and the Infinity-8B results as supporting transferability. New Appendix I discusses architectural tradeoffs, hypothesizes that diffusion denoising enlarges the search space, and declines to identify a superior architecture. The original spatial-alignment and untested-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents the first PCA component, model-specific resolutions and batch schedules, and reliance on Infinity's public defaults. Appendix G.2 identifies A800-SXM4-80GB hardware and memory-driven inference handling. These are useful implementation disclosures; the algorithm pseudocode and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to DreamVideo, MeshXL, discriminative codebook priors, and VARGPT-v1.1, while removing the CLIP-latent generation paper, Wan, FreeScale, and a foundation-model reasoning survey. Appendix I adds qualified positioning against diffusion scaling. The principal novelty claim and related-work organization remain.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain. v2 inserts a user-study subsection, settings and analysis appendices, acknowledgements, and a NeurIPS conference footer, with local wording and terminology edits. The accompanying renumbering and additions do not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with dedicated human-study, Infinity-8B, DPG-Bench, diversity, runtime/memory, and clustering-control tables. It expands Table 1 and the temperature table. Figure 2 is redrawn with additional curves, TFLOPs units, and one-based scale labels; several retained figures and tables are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct output-diversity measurements, human preference evidence, and a clustering-versus-random-dropping control with resampling retained. v2 adds these targeted tests, substantially strengthening support for its central diversity and selection claims, alongside broader model evaluation and practical resource measurements. The small user study, timing exclusion of decoding, and absent uncertainty estimates limit the gains; the new Equation 1 indexing error also reduces precision. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantially stronger experimental validation.
